reasons: Datadog query sum:redis.clients.blocked sums the blocked-client count across all series, but the candidate uses avg(), which divides the total by the series count and gives a different number. The PromQL should use sum().

The $host template variable has prefix host and default *, so it should become a matcher on the host label (for example host_name=~"$host"). The candidate drops it, so it selects a different set of series. The dataset lists no host label among observed labels, so the exact label name needs confirming before the matcher is written.
The metric is an OTel sum with monotonic false, so an up-down counter and no rate() is correct; quantity and unit ({client}) match the Datadog count of blocked clients.
$scope has no prefix and default *, so dropping it is correct; $key is not used by the query and is ignored.
